description.text: Pope Evaristus served as bishop of Rome from around 99 to 107 CE, a period that overlapped the final years of the Apostolic Age. According to the Liber Pontificalis and Eusebius, he was a Greek born in Bethlehem to a Jewish father named Judah, and he assumed the papacy in the third year of Emperor Trajan’s reign, holding office for roughly nine years before his death.

During his episcopate, Evaristus is credited with formalizing the public celebration of marriage under priestly blessing, a practice that would become a cornerstone of Catholic sacramental life. He is also described as being "crowned with martyrdom" in the Liber Pontificalis, though the Roman Martyrology lists him without a martyr title; he was interred in the catacomb beneath Saint Peter’s Basilica, close to the apostle’s own burial site.

curiosities.text: Evaristus decreed that marriage should be celebrated publicly and with the blessing of a priest, establishing a precedent for the Catholic sacrament of marriage.
He is described in the Liber Pontificalis as being "crowned with martyrdom", though the Roman Martyrology does not list him as a martyr.
He was buried near the body of Saint Peter in the Vatican, in Saint Peter's tomb under Saint Peter's Basilica.
